items.rationale: The indoor supply leak triggers escape-of-water cover under §2.4.2. Necessary pinpointing and the first call-out on this invoice are covered under §7.1.7(e)–(f); the comparable combined charge is €680 gross.

items.description: Kitchen floor and wall-base moisture measurement
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(e) covers measurements needed to establish the extent of moisture from the leak. The gross benchmark for this survey is €164.
Sections 7.1.7(e) and (g) cover necessary diagnostic labour at customary rates, provided it does not duplicate the separately billed tasks. The supplied gross benchmark for all 14 hours is €1,305.

Section 7.1.7(f) allows only the first travel, mileage or call-out charge on this contractor's invoice; line 1 already includes the call-out. If line 1 were treated solely as a diagnostic charge, the vehicle benchmark would be €83 gross.
Opening the wall and freeing the failed indoor supply pipe are necessary to repair it under §§2.4.3 and 7.1.7(a). The gross benchmark for this access work is €138.

items.description: Remove and dispose of soaked pipe insulation
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(a) covers removal and disposal of the two affected sections of lagging. At €72 gross each, the whole-line estimate is €144.

items.description: Repair confirmed leak at copper tee
items.rationale: Sections 2.4.3 and 7.1.1(b) support the local repair of the failed supply pipe. Allow about €150 gross for the repair work, excluding the materials billed on line 8.

items.description: Replacement copper section and standard lagging
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.7(c) and 7.1.9 cover like-for-like materials. Allow €105 gross for the short same-size copper section, tee and ordinary foam lagging, excluding the repair labour.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) require moisture attributable to this event; the old chimney stain is unrelated. If loss-related moisture were established, a small-area drying service would be about €100 gross.
Sections 7.1.7(b) and (e) cover necessary equipment hire for the documented kitchen moisture. The gross benchmark for one dryer is €51.

items.description: Dry kitchen floor and wall base
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(b) covers drying the affected floor and wall base. Allow €102 gross for the drying service, without counting the separately billed dryer hire again under §7.1.8(c).
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) and (e) do not cover equipment used on unrelated historic moisture damage. If the fans were needed for this loss, the benchmark would be 2 × €27, or €54 gross.

items.description: Clean up the kitchen repair area
items.rationale: Section 5.2.1 and the exception in §7.1.8(a) cover removal of repair dust and offcuts, not general housekeeping. The gross benchmark for the local cleanup is €82.
This is the first and only travel charge on the drying contractor's invoice and supports covered kitchen drying under §7.1.7(f). Allow €83 gross.

Sections 3.5, 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(a) exclude general housekeeping and work in unaffected rooms; the covered kitchen cleanup is already on line 13. A conditional gross estimate for the whole-flat service is €230.

items.description: Remove, transport and dispose of damaged table
items.rationale: The indoor table is insured furnishing under §4.2.6; §7.1.7(h) and §5.2.1 cover removal, hauling and disposal. The whole-line gross benchmark is 3 × €56 = €168, separate from the table's current value.

items.description: Collect, deliver and assemble replacement table
items.rationale: Section 7.1.7(h) expressly covers delivery and setup even though the policyholder bought the table directly. Allow €152 gross for the service; the current-value deduction under §7.1.1(d) concerns the table itself.

The year-round outdoor furniture is not indoor furnishing under §4.2.6, and §7.1.8(f) excludes inspection of items unaffected by the kitchen leak. If covered, a brief inspection would be about €50 gross.
